declarations.docstring: The dual of an algebra over its base ring, equipped with the module action induced by right multiplication in the algebra.
Two elements of the right algebra dual are equal when their associated functionals agree on every algebra element.
The additive commutative group structure on the right algebra dual.
The base-ring, algebra, and right-dual scalar actions form a scalar tower.
The base-ring module structure on the right algebra dual.
The algebra module structure on the right algebra dual.
The scalar action of the algebra on its right dual.
The base-ring and algebra scalar actions on the right dual commute.
An algebra submodule of the right dual is closed under scalar multiplication by the base ring.
The linear equivalence from the right algebra dual to the ordinary module dual.
The functional associated with a sum evaluates as the sum of the evaluations.
The functional associated with a base scalar multiple evaluates as the corresponding scalar multiple.
The algebra action on the right dual evaluates by right multiplication of the argument.
The zero element of the right dual evaluates to zero.
The proposition that a module is generated by a single vector.
The proposition that a vector generates its module.
The complex square-zero extension algebra with a two-dimensional nilpotent summand.
The ideal of two-variable complex polynomials generated by terms of total degree at least two.
The ideal generated by terms of degree at least two is the square of the ideal generated by the variables.
The degree-at-least-two ideal is spanned by homogeneous polynomials of degree at least two.
The right algebra dual of the square-zero plane algebra.
An algebra equivalence between the square-zero plane algebra and the quotient by the degree-at-least-two ideal.
The first nilpotent basis element corresponds to the image of the first polynomial variable in the quotient.
The second nilpotent basis element corresponds to the image of the second polynomial variable in the quotient.
The complex basis of the square-zero plane algebra indexed by `Fin 3`.
The square-zero plane basis consists of one followed by the two nilpotent basis elements.
A dual functional that vanishes on the nilpotent summand is its value at one times the scalar-part dual element.
The square-zero plane algebra has complex finrank three.
The right dual of the square-zero plane algebra has complex finrank three.
The square-zero plane dual satisfies the displayed auxiliary module property but is not cyclic.
The square-zero plane algebra is finite as a complex module.
The square-zero plane dual is finite as a complex module.
The square-zero plane dual is nontrivial.
The square-zero plane dual satisfies the displayed auxiliary module property.
The linear map sending a pair of coefficients to the corresponding linear polynomial class in the quotient.
The linear-term map is the sum of the variable classes weighted by their coefficients.
The product of any two values of the linear-term map is zero.
One and the two nilpotent basis elements are linearly independent over the complex numbers.
The image in the quotient of a product of two polynomial variables is zero.
Multiplication in the square-zero plane algebra expands using the scalar parts and the nilpotent part of the right factor.
No singleton spans the square-zero plane dual as a module over the square-zero plane algebra.
The square-zero plane dual is not a cyclic module over the square-zero plane algebra.
An algebra homomorphism from the polynomial quotient to the square-zero plane algebra.
The composite from the square-zero plane algebra to the quotient and back is the identity.
A polynomial variable class maps to the corresponding coordinate vector in the nilpotent summand.
An auxiliary linear map from a pair of complex scalars into the square-zero plane dual, parameterized by a dual element.
A complex-linear equivalence from the square-zero plane algebra to the product of its scalar and two-dimensional nilpotent parts.
The action of an algebra element on a dual functional is the sum of scalar-part scaling and evaluation on the nilpotent part times the scalar-part dual element.
The cyclic span of a dual element is contained in the range of its associated auxiliary linear map.
The scalar-part dual element evaluates an algebra element to its scalar component.
An algebra homomorphism from the square-zero plane algebra to the polynomial quotient.
The composite from the polynomial quotient to the square-zero plane algebra and back is the identity.
The nilpotent summand maps to the corresponding linear polynomial class in the quotient.
The first distinguished nilpotent element of the square-zero plane algebra.
The square of the first distinguished nilpotent element is zero.
The product of the first and second distinguished nilpotent elements is zero.
The second distinguished nilpotent element of the square-zero plane algebra.
The product of the second and first distinguished nilpotent elements is zero.
The square of the second distinguished nilpotent element is zero.
The distinguished dual element that extracts the scalar part of the square-zero plane algebra.
Every nonzero submodule of the square-zero plane dual contains the scalar-part dual element.
The scalar-part dual element is nonzero.
For a nontrivial module, cyclicity is equivalent to the existence of a linear equivalence with a quotient of its coefficient ring by an ideal.
A nontrivial module is simple if and only if every nonzero vector is cyclic.
